summary: Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University (attested 2015) under John C. Huntington. In 2015, Choi was a Visiting Researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992). He also trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Ham studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and completed a PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Bangor University (~1928–1932) and Jesus College, Oxford (~1932–1935), later serving on the faculty at Bangor University (~1936–1955).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge. Ujeed serves as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees from Cambridge (~1970–1973) and Lancaster (~1978–1985). He held posts at St Martin's College (~1986–2007) and the University of Cumbria (~2007–2011).

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004. In 2005, he was a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute, Monash University.
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and trained under traditional teacher Sotan Oka.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Oxford (~1960–1963), he served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004).

Ian Reader is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983). His career includes positions at Lancaster University (~2000–2006) and the University of Manchester (~2006).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who completed a PhD in Archaeology at the University of Peshawar in 2007. Shah serves as Associate Professor and Chairman of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later held posts at Otani University Junior College (~1968–1973) and Otani University (~1973–2006).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, where he completed his doctorate in 1953, and later served as professor emeritus there (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani Universities under Kogen Mizuno. He held academic positions at Komazawa University from 1975 to 2013, serving as professor from 1985 onward.

Ichiro Numata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who holds lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University under Jitsuzo Kuwabara (~1922–1925) and later held a post at Kyoto University from ~1936 to 1965.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was an academic who studied at Sapienza University of Rome and served as a professor there from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1941) and held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (~1943–1952) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1960–1998).

Ihsan Ali is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Peshawar (~1974–1978) and under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1989–1993). He later served as Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).
Ikko Arai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Komazawa University, having studied under MA supervisor Shiro Matsumoto.
